Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides an introductory guide to setting up an e-commerce SMS marketing channel within Klaviyo, covering platform configuration, list growth via two-step pop-ups, campaign cadence, flow restrictions, and core performance KPIs. modules: [EML] topics: [SMS marketing, list growth, campaign strategy] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. SMS marketing / Implementing a foundational SMS marketing channel for e-commerce brands, utilizing platforms like Klaviyo to consolidate email and SMS operations. Managing technical and compliance constraints: adhering to the 160-character limit per message to avoid double billing, recognizing the high cost of MMS (images) compared to standard text, restricting abandonment flows to a single compliant message, and observing legal "quiet hours" (e.g., avoiding sends before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m.). list growth / Expanding the SMS subscriber base by separating email and SMS opt-ins into a two-step pop-up flow to minimize friction. Using clear, action-oriented copy for the SMS step, such as "finish signing up with text to activate 20% off," to maximize conversion rates without offering additional discounts beyond the initial email incentive. campaign strategy / Structuring an SMS campaign calendar centered around high-impact, direct events (e.g., flash sales, restocks, new product launches) rather than broad nurture content. Maintaining a low frequency of 1 to 2 SMS campaigns per week to prevent high unsubscribe rates, testing optimal send times (typically late morning or early afternoon), and shifting performance evaluation away from vanity metrics (open rates) toward click rates (aiming for 5–15%) and unsubscribe rates (maintaining below 1%).

Look for. The recommended time delay for website pop-ups: 6 to 10 seconds after page load. The primary compliance rule regarding SMS abandonment flows: you are only allowed to send one SMS message per abandonment flow. The key SMS KPIs to monitor: target a click rate of 5–15% and keep the unsubscribe rate below 1%. The legal limitation on SMS send times: avoiding sends prior to 8:00 a.m. and post 9:00 p.m.
